clue.text: Opportunity out east to have the horse inside the coach

indicators.note: inside says the horse is placed within what remains of the opportunity word
out says the compass letter is dropped from the word for opportunity

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A chance is missed, and a horse ends up riding inside a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops E from CHANCE, leaving CHANC; 'inside' puts ARAB within it, after CH. A charabanc is an old open-topped motor coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an early motor bus used for outings, a kind of coach.

clue.text: Space traveller's eccentric aunt supporting Archbishop Lang

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so the archbishop's name comes first

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942

indicators.note: eccentric signals that the letters of aunt are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eccentric aunt props up a famous archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' turns AUNT into NAUT, placed below COSMO ('supporting' in a down clue). Cosmo Gordon Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmonaut is a Soviet or Russian astronaut, one who journeys into space.

clue.text: Allow many into the mine entrance

indicators.note: into says the letter for many goes inside the word for a mine entrance

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: Lots of people are let into the mouth of a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to allow them in, or to let something be the case.

clue.text: Write comments below article — not in neat letters

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means the rest follows the article

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in says the word not goes inside the rearranged neat
letters suggests the word neat is respelt as a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Notes are to be written under an article, and not in tidy handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' rearranges NEAT as NATE, and 'in' puts NOT inside it after the first N, giving NNOTATE, placed 'below' A in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To annotate a text is to add explanatory notes to it.

clue.text: Farm animal — unusually shy, rare one

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A timid and rare creature is spotted on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges SHY, RARE and I together. An Ayrshire is a breed of dairy cattle from south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayrshires are a Scottish breed of dairy cattle kept on farms.

clue.text: Newspaper article capitally upholding Nelson

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece praises Nelson in capital letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's Column in London, the capital, holds up the statue of Admiral Nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular newspaper feature is a column; in London a tall pillar holds up the admiral's statue.

clue.text: Musician born in Glenrothes, possibly?

explanation.surface: A musician hails from a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Glenrothes is a town in Fife, Scotland, so a native is a Fifer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fife player is a musician, and a native of Fife in Scotland shares the name.

clue.text: Toadstool providing a Theatre Cat with sport at first

indicators.note: at first says the word for sport is placed before the cat's name

parts.note: sport can mean fun, as in making sport of someone
Gus the Theatre Cat is a character in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats

explanation.surface: A toadstool somehow gives a theatrical cat a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Gus is Eliot's Theatre Cat, the poem set in the musical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadstool is a mushroom-like growth, a kind of fungal fruiting body.

clue.text: Soldiers carried in one aircraft or another

definitions.note: here another means a second kind of aircraft

indicators.note: carried in says the soldiers are put inside the aircraft word

parts.note: a fighter is one type of military aircraft
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are flown in one aircraft or other.
explanation.walkthrough: Put RE into FIGHTER, one aircraft, and you get another: a freighter, a cargo plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo aircraft, a different type from a fighter.

clue.text: Additional clause describing Paul Revere

explanation.surface: An extra clause is added about Paul Revere.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere made a famous midnight ride in 1775, warning of British troops.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment appended to a document is a rider; Revere is famed as a horseman on his midnight ride.

clue.text: Discussion group for new marines

indicators.note: new suggests the word marines is made fresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A discussion group is set up for newly recruited marines.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a class or meeting for discussion of a topic.

clue.text: An oil producer was untruthful about several points

indicators.note: about says the lie word goes round the compass points

parts.note: lied means was untruthful
N, S and E are compass points

explanation.surface: An oil company is accused of lying about several issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LIED around NSE, three points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed is the seed of flax, pressed to yield linseed oil.

clue.text: Work for players enumerated in 7

explanation.surface: A piece for musicians is numbered in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is FREIGHTER, which has EIGHT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece composed for eight musicians is an octet, and eight is the number written within 7-down.

clue.text: Dish for woman accepting food mother rejected

indicators.note: accepting says the woman word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: her refers to a woman

indicators.note: rejected means the food and mother words are turned back to front

parts.note: grub is slang for food
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A woman takes some food that her mother refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns GRUB plus MA into AMBURG, which HER takes in ('accepting').
explanation.definitionFit: A hamburger is a dish of minced beef in a bun.

clue.text: Defensive cover for a king well thought out

parts.note: R, from rex, stands for king
a mature plan is one carefully considered

explanation.surface: Protection for a monarch has been carefully planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Armature is an old word for armour, protective covering for body or plant.

clue.text: Plant was witch's trophy of the Tam O'Shanter chase

definitions.text: witch's trophy of the Tam O'Shanter chase

explanation.surface: A plant was the witch's prize in Burns's famous chase.
explanation.walkthrough: In Burns's poem Tam o' Shanter, the witch Nannie pulls off the tail of Tam's mare Meg as he escapes over a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's-tail is a water plant; in the poem the witch seizes the horse's tail as her prize.

clue.text: Very small thing carried by sea to Morocco

indicators.note: carried by says the answer is borne within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something tiny is shipped by sea to Morocco.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is a minute particle, the smallest unit of an element.

clue.text: Singularly not a stereotyped form of madness?

definitions.text: Singularly not a stereotyped form of madness?

parts.words: Singularly not a stereotyped form of madness?
parts.note: an obsession fixed on a single subject: a madness of one thing, 'singularly' hinting at the Greek for one

explanation.surface: An unusual mental condition is described in a quirky way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singularly' points to MONO (one) and 'madness' to MANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Monomania is obsessive preoccupation with a single thing, a mental fixation.

clue.text: Initially this is brawny in athletes

definitions.text: Initially this is brawny in athletes

parts.words: Initially this is brawny in athletes
parts.note: the first letters of these five words spell TIBIA, the Latin name for the leg bone at the front of the shin

explanation.surface: A remark about athletes' brawny legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of 'this is brawny in athletes' give TIBIA, which is the bone itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the large front bone of the lower leg.

clue.text: Sounding-lead — a 19 in the plant

parts.note: a plumb is a lead weight on a line for sounding depth
19 is TURN, and a turn is a go

explanation.surface: A sounding-lead takes a turn in the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is TURN; taking a turn is having a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago, or leadwort, is a flowering plant; the word also means graphite.

clue.text: Circus' act that gives us a shock

explanation.surface: A circus performance gives the audience a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'turn' is a stage act, and a fright 'gives you a turn'.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's spot on the bill is their act; a sudden fright is said to give you one.

clue.text: The New Forest issue?

parts.note: issue means offspring, and Marryat's novel The ... of the New Forest names them

explanation.surface: A local problem in the New Forest, a woodland area in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue looks like a problem but means offspring; Frederick Marryat's 1847 novel is The Children of the New Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for offspring, a person's sons and daughters.

clue.text: Fellow land-owner in Europe formerly supplying pigment

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning fellow, as in co-worker
a Balt was one of the German land-owning class in the former Baltic provinces

explanation.surface: A colleague who once owned land in Europe provides colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Baltic Germans, or Balts, held estates in Estonia and Latvia before 1918.
explanation.definitionFit: Compounds of the metal give cobalt blue, a deep blue colouring.

clue.text: Cleopatra's poisoner caught, the general napping

indicators.note: caught says the snake word holds the general inside it

parts.note: Cleopatra killed herself with the bite of an asp
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: The snake that killed Cleopatra catches a general dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone napping is sleeping, dozing off.

clue.text: Mayfair's transgression, keeping a prisoner in this state?

indicators.note: keeping says the Mayfair and sin pieces hold the prisoner between them
in completes the container signal: the prisoner is kept inside

parts.note: W1 is the London postcode for Mayfair, read as WI, plus the possessive S
a sin is a transgression
a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A Mayfair sin of locking up a prisoner puts one in a certain state.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is a smart London district with postcode W1; read as letters, Mayfair's gives WIS. 'keeping ... in' puts CON between WIS and SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: But -few of these countryfolk, surely, decamp without paying

explanation.surface: Surely hardly any rural people do a runner from their bills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh are the people of Wales; to welsh is to run off without paying a debt. 'But few of these, surely' is the setter's tongue-in-cheek aside.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Wales share the name with a verb meaning to dodge a debt or bet.

clue.text: Polite form of address for mothers?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A courteous way to speak to mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mothers' gives two mothers: MA and DAM, a female parent of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a respectful way of addressing a woman.

clue.text: Verdi's abnormal capacity for getting things done.

indicators.note: abnormal suggests the composer's name is put into an irregular order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: The composer Verdi had an unusual ability to get things done.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is energy and determination to achieve goals.

clue.text: Escaped charge for disclosure of secrets

explanation.surface: Electricity escapes and secrets come out.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric current lost through poor insulation is leakage, and unauthorised release of information also bears the name.

clue.text: Hunter seen around at this address?

indicators.note: around says the hunter's name goes round the word at

parts.note: Orion is the great hunter of Greek myth, also a constellation

explanation.surface: A hunter is seen near this address.
explanation.walkthrough: Orion is the Hunter of Greek myth and the constellation; 'address' means a speech, not a location.
explanation.definitionFit: An address here is a formal speech, delivered to an audience.

clue.text: Ambassador returned to Libyan capital as a slave

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: returned says the word to and the capital letter are read backwards
capital means the first letter of the word Libyan

explanation.surface: An ambassador is sent back to the Libyan capital as a slave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' takes L from Libyan, and 'returned' turns TO plus L into LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf of ancient Sparta, hence any person in bondage.

clue.text: In a US state he meets presumably only women prodigies

indicators.note: In says the following pieces sit inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania
if there are no men, presumably only women are present

explanation.surface: A man in an American state finds himself among women only, a marvel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts HE plus NO MEN inside PA, Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable things or people, marvels.
